description: The dotnet CLI's build, clean, publish and restore switches across asm projects, as a .NET developer uses them: a RID in a project or a publish profile reaches the static library the program links, an artifacts path and -o move every output and dotnet clean takes all of them away again, the arch, os and use-current-runtime switches build the RID they name, and restore's lock file holds. Every path is this machine's RID or one named outright, so the same steps run on every build machine.

steps.description: ProgMusl names linux-musl-x64 in its own project, an ordinary property that no referenced project inherits: the SDK hands the RID to Shared itself, so the static library is built for that RID and linked (0.4.0 built Shared for this machine only, and the link failed with undefined symbol: mul_ints).

The publish profile's RuntimeIdentifier decides the build, as -r would (0.4.0 imported the profile after choosing the RIDs: it published this machine's RID into a RID folder and warned ASM0013), and its PublishDir where the program goes. Shared gets the profile's RID too.
An artifacts path moves every project's output into art/, in .NET's layout: the library's RID build under a debug_<rid> pivot, and the app's copy of it where the app loads it.
The app runs from the artifacts path and finds the library there.
The solution builds every project for this machine.
The program runs the static library's mul_ints(6, 7).
dotnet clean takes away what the build wrote, the RID outer build's own Lib.h and Lib.api.json included (0.4.0 left both behind: that build never recorded them for clean).
A rebuild (Clean, then Build) of the library alone.
The app builds without building its references, and still gets the library the earlier step built.
The arch switch builds this OS's RID for the other CPU, which any build machine can build.
The os switch builds Linux for this CPU.

The use-current-runtime switch publishes this machine's RID as -r would: the program directly in the folder, and no ASM0013 (0.4.0 published a RID folder and warned, which these scenarios' warnings-as-errors makes a failure).
-o moves the library's outputs, each RID's into a folder of its own.
dotnet clean with the same -o finds them again.
A static graph build (MSBuild's -graph) of the whole solution.
Restore writes a lock file for an asm project too.
A locked restore agrees with it.
And so does a build that restores in locked mode.
